title: Somatic cells can be modeled as a slow neural-like network obeying brain-like dynamics

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Somatic cells can be modeled as a slow neural-like network obeying brain-like dynamics

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The authors propose conceptualizing the link between gap junctional connectivity among planarian cells and discrete regenerative outcomes by viewing the cells as a neural-like network that processes developmental information more slowly but obeys the same statistical dynamics as the brain.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, we propose that one way to conceptualize the linkage between bioelectrical connectivity among worm cells (GJC) and discrete global behavioral outcomes achieved by regeneration is to view the worms’ cells as a neural-like network, processing developmental information more slowly but obeying the same statistical dynamics rules as are known to occur in the brain (Figure 9A).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “3. Discussion › 3.7. A hypothesis: Physiological Network Attractors Underlie Regions of Anatomical Morphospace”. Scope: Planarian somatic cell networks during regeneration

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-18: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.27

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim can be made measurable through system identification, but the necessary planarian network recordings do not exist in the source study. Current anatomy and static voltage images cannot test equivalence of statistical dynamics.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Record dense somatic bioelectric time series and compare fitted statistical-dynamics models with matched neural networks using predefined attractor, correlation, and transition statistics. The same model class must predict held-out perturbation responses in both systems.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The term neural-like permits several competing operationalizations.

Similarity can depend strongly on the chosen statistical description.

No dense planarian somatic-network time series is available.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.45
data adequacy: 0.05
analysis feasibility: 0.25
data existence: 0.1

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: This is a suggested conceptualization of gap-junction connectivity and regenerative outcomes. Without a named shared statistic, neural recordings and planarian voltage images can always be described either as the same dynamics or as merely analogous. The proposal does not set a distinguishing observation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The proposal asks the reader to treat somatic cells as a slower neural-like network obeying the brain's statistical dynamics. No statistic is named that would accept that description and reject an ordinary physiological network with the same coupling.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Which brain statistics are supposed to match is unspecified.

A slower non-neural gap-junction network fits the same regenerative outcomes.
